title: Resume a VCF Automation day-2 action sweep across an access-token expiry
prompt:
Implement `src/VcfAutomation/VcfAutomation.psm1`, the body of the `VcfAutomation` PowerShell 7 module for VCF Automation in VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1. Do not add files or edit any other file. The fixed manifest `src/VcfAutomation/VcfAutomation.psd1` exports only `Invoke-VcfaDeploymentActionSweep`; the implementation must use PowerShell's built-in HTTP and JSON facilities and must not require or vendor another module.

VCF Automation is the successor to vRealize and Aria Automation and has no specification in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository. The protected `docs/contract.json` was therefore transcribed by hand from the Broadcom xAPIs reference documentation, and says so plainly; `docs/official_sources.json` records every page URL, the operation it documents and the date it was fetched. Honor exactly the three operations the contract names — `getAccessToken`, `getDeployments` and `submitDeploymentActionRequest` — and call no other route.

Keep the supplied parameter block of `Invoke-VcfaDeploymentActionSweep` unchanged: `-ApiEndpoint`, `-Tenant`, `-ApiToken`, `-AccessToken`, `-ActionId`, `-Reason`, `-Inputs`, `-PageSize` and `-TimeoutSec`.

Behavior:

- Page through `getDeployments` from page 0 and collect every page before submitting any action request. Stop when the response envelope reports the last page; never request a page past it.
- Submit one `submitDeploymentActionRequest` per deployment, in ascending deployment-name order.
- Return one object per deployment, in that same ascending name order, carrying exactly the properties `DeploymentId`, `DeploymentName`, `RequestId` and `Status`. `RequestId` and `Status` come from the accepted request's `id` and `status`.
- The access token expires once three authorized calls have succeeded, so the second action request is refused with HTTP 401. Only a 401 from `submitDeploymentActionRequest` may trigger recovery. On that first 401, call `getAccessToken` exactly once, replace the access token with the issued `access_token`, and resend the identical interrupted request. Do not replay a page or an action request that already succeeded, refresh pre-emptively or a second time, refresh for any other status or operation, or retry a second 401.
- Raise a terminating error on any other transport or HTTP failure, or on a malformed response. For response data used by the sweep, a deployment page must contain an array-valued `content`, a Boolean `last`, and nonblank string `id` and `name` values for every deployment; an accepted action request must contain nonblank string `id` and `status` values; and a successful token response must contain a nonblank string `access_token`. Neither the returned objects nor any error message may contain either token.

Honor the exact wire contract:

- `getDeployments` is a bodyless GET carrying one `Authorization: Bearer ...` header and no `Content-Type`. Its query is exactly `page` then `size`, and `page` is sent explicitly on every request including page 0. Omit every other documented query member: `sort`, `ids`, `search`, `name`, `status`, `projects`, `resourceTypes`, `cloudAccounts`, `cloudTypes`, `requestedBy`, `ownedBy`, `tags`, `createdAt`, `expiresAt`, `lastUpdatedAt`, `expandResources`, `expandLastRequest`, `expandProject`, `expand`, `lastRequestStatus`, `deleted`, `$top`, `$skip`, `$orderby` and `$filter`. Omission means absent, never blank, zero, false, null, or a bare query delimiter.
- `submitDeploymentActionRequest` is a POST carrying one `Authorization: Bearer ...` header and a `Content-Type` of exactly `application/json` with no media-type parameters, and no query. Its body is compact JSON — no insignificant whitespace — with members in the contract order `actionId`, `inputs`, `reason`. An optional member the caller did not set is absent from the object, not `null`, not `""` and not `{}`.
- `getAccessToken` is a POST to `/tm/oauth/tenant/{tenant}/token` with a `Content-Type` of exactly `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, exactly one `Accept: application/json` header, no query, and no `Authorization` header at all — the API token is the credential and travels in the body. The body contains exactly `grant_type` then `refresh_token`; `grant_type` is the literal `refresh_token`; the API token is percent-encoded, so a literal `+` never appears in it and `/`, `=` and `&` are escaped.

Run `python3 -B .protected/verify.py`. The protected verifier starts contract-pinned loopback scenarios on ephemeral `127.0.0.1` ports and grades the returned artifacts, terminating errors, and flushed JSONL request logs. It covers the exact expiry/resume sequence, optional-member serialization, malformed responses, transport and HTTP failures, and forbidden refreshes. The mock serves only the operations named in `docs/contract.json` and never contacts a live VMware endpoint.

source_basis.specification_note: VCF Automation has no specification in vmware/vcf-api-specs and the xAPIs pages for these operations publish no machine-readable document, so docs/contract.json is derived from rendered reference documentation and states that plainly.

scenario: Two deployment pages and the first day-2 action request succeed, the second action request is refused with HTTP 401 because the access token has expired, getAccessToken issues a replacement once, and the identical interrupted request resumes before the final deployment is actioned.
constraint: The contract-pinned loopback request log proves exact optional-member omission, the absent Authorization header on the token exchange, token rotation, and resumption without replaying completed work.
